title: Scout Selection: Best Fantasy team for Gameweek 10
body:
There are double-ups on four clubs – Arsenal, Everton, Brighton & Hove Albion and AFC Bournemouth - in the best team for Gameweek 10 of Fantasy Premier League.

Although managers have been advised to move to four or five at the back for their strategies over the season, it’s worth bearing in mind that the Scout Selection is essentially a “Free Hit” side which is specific to each Gameweek and focuses far more on players with attacking upside. 

Both Everton and Arsenal are at home to promoted clubs; Toffees pair James Tarkowski (£6.2m) and Thierno Barry (£5.6m) face Coventry City in the first match of the Gameweek on Friday night, while Arsenal’s Gabriel (£8.0m) and Martin Odegaard (£6.7m) play Hull City at Emirates Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

On Sunday, Brighton’s Maxim De Cuyper (£5.4m) and Pascal Gross (£6.2m) are at home to Brentford, while Bournemouth’s Djordje Petrovic (£4.5m) and Marcus Tavernier (£6.6m) visit Ipswich Town.

Mancheter City's Erling Haaland (£15.8m) and Liverpool's Alexander Isak (£9.2m) are named captain and vice-captain respectively.

Djordje Petrovic (AFC Bournemouth) £4.5m

The Bournemouth goalkeeper has stepped up his output recently after starting the season with a tough run of opponents. Petrovic has kept all of his three clean sheets in 2026/27 over the last three Gameweeks, amassing 19 points in the process. 

Gabriel (Arsenal) £8.0m

His many routes to points have helped Arsenal’s Brazilian into second spot in the defender standings, despite only scoring once. Gabriel has earned six clean sheets and a team-high eight defensive contribution (DC) points, while his total of three headed shots from set-pieces is also more than any other Gunners player. 

James Tarkowski (Everton) £6.2m

Everton’s centre-back sits joint-seventh in the overall player standings thanks to his consistent run of points returns. Tarkowski has blanked just once across his nine appearances, producing a goal, an assist, four clean sheets and 10 DC points. 

Maxim De Cuyper (Brighton) £5.4m

A move into midfield for Brighton this season has helped the Belgian top the overall player standings thanks to his impact at both ends of the pitch. Listed as a defender in Fantasy, De Cuyper has combined two goals and four assists with six clean sheets to collect 69 points.

Morgan Rogers (Chelsea) £8.2m

Five goals and an assist in his first nine matches for Chelsea have made Rogers the most-popular midfielder in Fantasy, boasting an ownership of 52 per cent. He visits a Sunderland side who sit bottom of the table, having conceded at least twice in all but one of their last six league matches. 

Martin Odegaard (Arsenal) £6.7m

Rested from European duties in midweek, the Arsenal captain look set to return to their starting line-up against Hull. Odegaard has scored both his goals this season at Emirates Stadium, while in home matches, his 12 shots, six shots in the box and nine chances created rank top or joint-top among team-mates. 

Marcus Tavernier (AFC Bournemouth) £6.6m

His away form suggests the Bournemouth midfielder can deliver a big haul against Ipswich, who are yet to keep a clean sheet this season. Tavernier has scored and collected 10 points in three of his four road trips in 2026/27.

Pascal Gross (Brighton) £6.2m

Brighton’s playmaker remains the top-scoring midfielder in Fantasy despite back-to-back blanks at Liverpool and Man City. Gross’ dominance of set-pieces and penalties has still helped him to three goals and six assists, averaging 6.7 points per match.

Erling Haaland (Man City) £15.8m

After suffering a rare blank at home to Brighton last weekend, Haaland was back on the scoresheet in Man City’s 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday night. Up against a Nottingham Forest side who sit second-bottom of the league, the Norwegian has to be backed with the captain’s armband.

Alexander Isak (Liverpool) £9.2m

Liverpool’s Swede also extended his prolific form in the UEFA Champions League midweek, emerging from the bench to score against Fenerbahce. Isak is a strong alternative for the captaincy at a Crystal Palace side who have conceded a league-high 21 goals in just nine matches. 

Thierno Barry (Everton) £5.6m

The Everton star’s improving form suggests he can be a great budget forward to rotate in and out of your team according to the fixtures. Having netted against promoted pair Ipswich and Hull over the last five Gameweeks, Barry is backed to score more goals at home to Coventry.
